title: Tencent WorkBuddy Doubles Alibaba and ByteDance Traffic
summary: Tencent's WorkBuddy AI agent recorded 85.34M monthly visits in September 2026, nearly doubling Alibaba's Qwen Office and ByteDance's Doubao Work combined.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Tencent's WorkBuddy recorded 85.34 million monthly visits in September 2026, roughly doubling Alibaba's 46.55 million and nearly tripling ByteDance's 30.39 million.
- Since launching in March 2026, WorkBuddy reached 50% of China's top 500 companies with 50,000+ developers and 200,000+ registered skills.
- Tencent Cloud's overseas AI demand grew triple digits year over year, with international customers doubling through aggressive cost competitiveness.


Tencent has pulled ahead in China's workplace AI agent market with WorkBuddy recording 85.34 million monthly visits in September 2026, according to Seoul Economic Daily. The figure puts Tencent roughly 1.8 times ahead of Alibaba's Qwen Office at 46.55 million visits and nearly 2.8 times ahead of ByteDance's Doubao Work at 30.39 million, establishing a commanding lead in the enterprise AI sector just months after launch.


The traffic numbers represent a dramatic reversal for Tencent, which industry observers had criticized as late as 2025 for falling behind rivals in the AI model race. WorkBuddy's rapid adoption signals a strategic pivot from raw model performance to revenue-generating AI applications.


## Market Penetration and Developer Adoption


Dowson Tong, senior executive vice president at Tencent, revealed at the company's Global Digital Ecosystem Summit in Shenzhen on October 29 that WorkBuddy has reached 50% of China's top 500 companies since its March 2026 launch. The platform now supports more than 50,000 developers and hosts over 200,000 registered skills across more than 50 industries.


Officially launched on March 2026, WorkBuddy benefited from a five to six month head start over competing workplace agents from Alibaba and ByteDance. Analysts attribute the widening gap to Tencent's accessibility strategy, which allows the service to run across desktop environments and WeChat without separate installation requirements.


## Deep Integration With WeChat Ecosystem


Tencent's competitive advantage stems from tight integration with WeCom, China's leading corporate messaging platform. WorkBuddy operates within WeCom to handle tasks around the clock, automatically passing results to colleagues through existing communication channels. The AI agent can access conversations, documents, and meeting records accumulated in WeCom, subject to approval limits, to understand context and execute complex workflows.


The platform connects disparate corporate systems including enterprise resource planning and customer relationship management tools, consolidating data processing in a single interface. In one example, WorkBuddy can organize multiple expense receipts and file a consolidated settlement request automatically, eliminating repetitive manual data entry across multiple systems.


## Overseas Expansion Driven by Cost Advantage


Tencent Cloud reported triple-digit year-over-year growth in overseas AI demand, with active international customers doubling over the past year. The company has won clients including German software firm Maxon, Romanian e-commerce platform eMAG, and CNN Brasil through aggressive cost competitiveness.


Tencent's pricing strategy allows customers to choose among multiple models depending on task requirements, including its own Hunyuan alongside third-party options like DeepSeek and Kimi. The company is accelerating optimization for domestically produced AI chips, achieving a fivefold throughput increase on Chinese-made semiconductors in just two weeks to lower inference costs further.


The company expanded its Frankfurt data center in March 2026 and plans to build or expand facilities across Asia, the Middle East, Europe, and the Americas over the next year. Tencent now operates more than 2 million servers worldwide to support explosive demand growth.


## Strategic Shift From Models to Agents


WorkBuddy represents a successful counterattack for a company that faced criticism over its Hunyuan language model trailing Alibaba's Qwen and ByteDance's Doubao in performance benchmarks throughout 2025. Tencent recruited Yao Shunyu, a key researcher formerly at OpenAI, in late 2025 to overhaul its AI operations.


The strategic pivot reflects a broader industry shift from improving model performance to building[AI agents](https://emergent.sh/learn/best-ai-agents-for-business) that generate actual revenue. Because agents consume vast token volumes while executing complex tasks, they offer clearer paths to monetization than general-purpose language models. Tencent's newer models have since ranked near the top in global web development evaluations and recorded the highest weekly token call volume.


## What This Means


Tencent's WorkBuddy success demonstrates that ecosystem integration and accessibility can trump raw model performance in enterprise AI adoption. The platform's lead over Alibaba and ByteDance suggests that workplace AI competition will be won through seamless workflow integration rather than benchmark scores alone. With overseas customers doubling and triple-digit demand growth, Tencent has transformed from an AI laggard into a formidable enterprise player, setting the template for how Chinese tech giants can monetize artificial intelligence through practical business applications rather than consumer-facing chatbots.
